title: Coral and the Extraction
premise: Oscar Nakamura walked away from a covert financial-intelligence unit after a botched operation left an informant dead, and now she launders nothing but clean money for a boutique firm, keeping her head down. When a burner phone arrives with no return address and a voice she buried three years ago—her presumed-dead handler, Marisol—Oscar learns the unit didn't disband; it went private, selling extraction services to cartels and oligarchs. To take the network down, Oscar must re-enter the world that trained her, rebuild trust with the only team she ever called family, and decide whether loyalty to the people she loved matters more than the truth of what they all did. In the end, Oscar exposes the network at a global compliance summit, Marisol sacrifices herself to give Oscar the final ledger, and Oscar chooses testimony over vengeance, finding a fragile new family among the survivors.
about_author: Lena Fairweather is the pen name of a former compliance analyst who spent a decade tracing money through shell companies before turning to fiction. She writes thrillers about people who know exactly where the bodies are buried—because they filed the paperwork.

chapters.title: Clean Hands
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV. Two years after leaving the unit, Oscar audits a charity's spotless books, insomnia-frayed and deliberately invisible. A small anomaly in a wire transfer pattern itches at skills she swore off. Emotional beat: the numb safety of her new life, and the first crack in it.

chapters.title: The Burner That Rings
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV. A package with no sender: a burner phone that rings at 3 a.m. The voice is Marisol's—her handler, dead three years by official record. Marisol warns her the unit is hunting its ghosts and gives her forty-eight hours to run. Emotional beat: dread and grief colliding; the past refusing to stay buried.

chapters.title: Ghosts of the Program
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV, with an intercut of Marisol's. Oscar verifies the voice against old case files and discovers three former colleagues have died in 'accidents' in six months. She digs out a hidden drive from her old life. Emotional beat: terror sharpening into resolve—she can't outrun this, so she'll face it.

chapters.title: Old Wounds, New Allies
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV. She tracks down Dev, the unit's former tech analyst, now paranoid and living off-grid. He refuses until she shows him the death pattern; then his fear turns to fury. They form an uneasy two-person cell. Emotional beat: the first fragile re-stitching of found family.

chapters.title: Extraction Protocol
chapters.summary: Marisol's POV. Flashback chapters reveal the unit's transformation: after disavowal, its director, Callum Reyes, privatized extraction—kidnapping witnesses, laundering their disappearances through clean finance. Marisol faked her death to infiltrate him. Emotional beat: the reader learns the machine's scale; Marisol's guilt mirrors Oscar's.

chapters.title: The Sum of Small Lies
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV. Oscar re-enters her old firm under pretext, planting Dev's malware on a client server tied to Reyes. A close call with a unit operative, Wren—someone she once loved—forces her to lie face-to-face. Emotional beat: loyalty versus truth made flesh; she deceives the person she trusted most.

chapters.title: What Marisol Buried
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Marisol contacts Oscar directly; a tense dead-drop meeting reveals the final ledger of every extraction, but Reyes suspects a mole. Marisol admits the dead informant from 'the incident' was her order, not Oscar's fault. Emotional beat: absolution, and the terrible cost of the truth.

chapters.title: Tightening the Net
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV. Reyes springs the trap: Wren arrests Dev, and Oscar is offered her old life back if she surrenders the ledger. She pretends to negotiate while Dev, in custody, stalls interrogation. Emotional beat: the darkest hour—family captured, the plan compromised, time expired.

chapters.title: The Extraction
chapters.summary: Oscar and Marisol's POV, converging. Oscar trades the ledger for Dev at a container terminal; Wren, confronted with proof of her own planned disposal, turns. Reyes corners Marisol, who triggers the ledger's broadcast to prosecutors and press before he can stop her. Emotional beat: sacrifice, betrayal reversed, loyalty finally aligned with truth.

chapters.title: What the Water Keeps
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV. Weeks later: Reyes in custody, Marisol dead but named, Oscar testifying under protection. She sleeps through the night for the first time, wakes to Dev making breakfast, and chooses to stay visible—testifying publicly rather than vanishing. Emotional beat: quiet, hard-won peace; justice outside the law, family rebuilt from ash.
